title: Tenali Raman Tale 140

full_text:
Two neighboring householders, Somu and Ramu, were locked in a bitter feud over a massive coconut palm tree.
The trunk of the tree grew in Somu’s garden, but its top branches leaned over the wall, hanging directly above Ramu’s tiled roof.
Whenever ripe coconuts fell, they smashed Ramu’s roof tiles; but whenever Ramu picked the fallen coconuts, Somu accused him of theft!
Somu claimed: 'The roots are in my soil; every coconut belongs to me!'
Ramu claimed: 'The nuts fall on my roof and break my tiles; they belong to me!'

They brought the dispute to King Krishnadevaraya, demanding that the tree either be chopped down or the other neighbor imprisoned.
The King referred the case to Tenali Raman.

Tenali inspected the coconut tree.
He said to both men:
'The law must divide the tree according to natural equity!
Since Somu owns the trunk and roots in his soil, Somu shall be the sole owner of the **lower half** of the tree from the roots up to the branches!
And since Ramu owns the airspace and suffers the broken tiles, Ramu shall be the sole owner of the **upper half** of the tree where the coconuts grow!'

Both men were delighted:
Ramu smiled, thinking he would get all the coconuts;
Somu smiled, thinking he owned the base.

Then Tenali announced the operational rules:
'Now, hear the law:
Somu, as owner of the lower trunk, must water the roots, fertilize the soil, and protect the trunk every single day! But he is strictly forbidden from climbing into Ramu’s upper half to touch a single coconut!
And Ramu, as owner of the upper half, may harvest all the coconuts! But he is strictly forbidden from touching Somu’s trunk with a ladder or stepping upon Somu’s bark to climb up!'

The two neighbors stared at each other in stunned silence.
Somu realized: 'If I water the tree, Ramu gets all the coconuts, and I get only hard labor!'
Ramu realized: 'If I cannot touch the trunk or lean a ladder against it, I cannot reach the coconuts at all!'

Tenali looked at them with a warm, gentle smile:
'Do you see the folly of your stubborn selfishness?
Nature created a tree as a single, harmonious living blessing. You cannot divide a living tree with anger without rendering it useless to both!
Now, shake hands:
Let Somu water the tree, let Ramu harvest the coconuts, and let both families share the sweet fruit equally, dividing the coconuts and sharing the cost of repairing the roof tiles!'

The two neighbors were deeply moved by Tenali’s wise counsel.
They embraced, dropped their lawsuits, and shared the harvests for decades in harmony and peace.
moral: Generosity and neighborly compromise yield sweet fruit; selfish litigation bears only legal thorns.
